# Third-party technical reference: Python OrderedDict LRU cache move_to_end get update eviction

Source: a community-maintained reference excerpt.

OrderedDict and LRU cache reference

An OrderedDict records insertion order. Assigning a new value to
an existing key does not automatically mark it as the most recent
key. move_to_end(key) moves an existing item to the newest end.
popitem(last=False) removes the oldest item. An LRU policy treats
successful reads and writes as accesses; a cache miss does not
count as an inserted value.

A stored None, zero, False, or empty string is still a cache hit.
A membership check distinguishes an absent key from these values.
Updating an existing item should not consume extra capacity.

{"command": "cd /workspace/reference_work && python3 -c "
from normalize_order import normalize_order
import copy

# provided example
row = {'id':'o1','customer':'north','paid':True,'amount':1200,'refunded':200}
exp = {'order_id':'o1','customer_id':'north','state':'settled','gross_cents':1200,'refund_cents':200}
got = normalize_order(row)
assert got == exp, got
assert isinstance(got, dict) and got is not row

# pending case, zero refund, extra keys ignored, input not mutated
row2 = {'id':'o2','customer':'south','paid':False,'amount':500,'refunded':0,'extra':'x'}
snap = copy.deepcopy(row2)
got2 = normalize_order(row2)
assert got2 == {'order_id':'o2','customer_id':'south','state':'pending','gross_cents':500,'refund_cents':0}, got2
assert row2 == snap, 'input mutated'

# falsy paid values -> pending
assert normalize_order({'id':'a','customer':'b','paid':0,'amount':0,'refunded':0})['state']=='pending'
# full refund keeps gross and refund separate
assert normalize_order({'id':'a','customer':'b','paid':True,'amount':300,'refunded':300}) == {'order_id':'a','customer_id':'b','state':'settled','gross_cents':300,'refund_cents':300}
# fresh dict each call
r = {'id':'a','customer':'b','paid':True,'amount':1,'refunded':0}
assert normalize_order(r) is not normalize_order(r)
print('all tests passed')
""}
